lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: specifying a sequence of transformations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Reflect the point (-1, -2) across the x-axis. Give the image.
Rotate the point (-5, -1) counterclockwise about the origin by 90°. Give the image.
A regular polygon has 3 sides. How many rotations about its centre, strictly between 0° and 360°, carry it onto itself, and what is the smallest such angle?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(7, -5) and B(-5, -7). After a transformation the images are A′(-7, 5) and B′(5, 7), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Point P(10, -4) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 2, y + 8). Give the image P′.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
